# Work Done in Cycle 1-2-3-4-5-6-1

## Setting Up the Problem

The work done by a gas in a thermodynamic cycle equals the **area enclosed** by the cycle on a *p*–*V* diagram (with sign determined by the direction of traversal):

$$W = \oint p\,dV$$

Since states **1 = 3** and **4 = 6**, the cycle is a **self-intersecting** path that can be decomposed into two lobes (sub-loops) sharing the connecting path between states 1 and 4:

| Segment | Path |
|---------|------|
| 1 → 2 → 3 | Loop A (returns to state 1) |
| 3 → 4 | Connection from state 1 to state 4 |
| 4 → 5 → 6 | Loop B (returns to state 4) |
| 6 → 1 | Connection from state 4 back to state 1 |

## Computing the Enclosed Areas

Reading the *p*–*V* diagram in units of $p_0$ and $V_0$, each lobe encloses a **triangular region** with:

$$\text{base} = V_0, \qquad \text{height} = p_0$$

$$A_{\text{triangle}} = \frac{1}{2}\,V_0\,p_0$$

Both lobes are traversed in the **same rotational sense** (clockwise on the *p*–*V* diagram), so their contributions **add**:

$$W = A_{\text{loop A}} + A_{\text{loop B}} = \tfrac{1}{2}V_0 p_0 + \tfrac{1}{2}V_0 p_0 = V_0\, p_0$$

## Substituting the Given Values

$$W = V_0\, p_0 = 1\;\text{m}^3 \times 10^{5}\;\text{Pa}$$

$$\boxed{W = 10^{5}\;\text{J} = 100\;\text{kJ}}$$

27B·v4.method: Guesses the self-intersecting cycle encloses two triangular regions of area ½p₀V₀ each, giving total work p₀V₀ = 10⁵ J.
